structure: Part 5, Commodity search and consignment details, read in full at repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend main 4c2119da under src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities: page.js (three page ids and slugs), evaluation.js (the commodity line and unit obligation bindings), copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js (search and consignmentDetails keys claimed here; identification keys belong to part 6), the search folder (search.controller.js, search.njk, matching.js, actions/commit-selection.js, selection/keys.js, line-key.js, selected-keys.js, view-model/selected-summary.js, legend.js, species-label.js, commodity-groups.js), the consignment-details folder (consignment-details.controller.js, consignment-details.njk, fields.js, lines.js, _selected-commodities-table.njk, _species-quantities.njk, remove/post-remove.js, remove/actions.js, view-model/selected-rows.js, groups.js, values.js, validation/count-drop.js) and the fit folder (search.fit.spec.js, 13 tests; consignment-details.fit.spec.js, 18 tests counting the four generated invalid-quantity tests; axe.js). Two pages are covered: the commodity search page at /commodities (heading, inset, search box with a 3-character minimum, word-prefix and code-prefix matching, results grouped per commodity with one tick box per species, carried selections, the N selected panel with Clear all, the commodity-code help details, the select-a-commodity error, and what saving writes and where it goes) and the Commodity details page at /consignment-details (empty-load redirect, the Selected commodities table with commodity-level and, for code 01061900, species-level Remove, Add another commodity, per-commodity and per-species headings, number of animals and number of packages fields with their validation, the count-drop rule against identifier records, and save). To state which commodities ask for packages and which are listed species by species, services/commodities/index.js and stub.js were consulted for the helpers these pages call; claims resting on them are marked inferred. Welsh copy was read for parity only. Unit tests (*.test.js) were left out per the partition.

claims.statement: A secondary 'Search' button submits the form with action 'search', which re-renders the page with the query and the current selection kept, without saving anything.
The search query is trimmed of surrounding whitespace, and results are listed only when the trimmed query is at least 3 characters long.
claims.quote:
export const MIN_SEARCH_LENGTH = 3

export const normaliseQuery = (value) => String(value ?? '').trim()

export const isSearchable = (query) =>
  normaliseQuery(query).length >= MIN_SEARCH_LENGTH

claims.statement: On first load the search page lists no commodities or tick boxes: the page lists nothing of its own accord until a long-enough query is entered.

Empty until the query is long enough — the

claims.statement: A query matches a commodity name or species label when its words, case-insensitively and split on any non-alphanumeric character, are a consecutive run of word-prefixes in that text (so 'tau' matches 'Bos taurus' and 'bos tau' matches only in that order).
claims.quote:
A query matches text when its words are a run of word-prefixes in that text.
 * So 'tau' matches 'Bos taurus' on its second word, and 'bos tau' matches only
 * where the two words run in that order.

claims.statement: A query also matches a commodity when the commodity code starts with the query (so '010' narrows to the 0101/0102 range).
claims.quote:
Commodity codes are digit strings, so they match on prefix rather than on
 * whole words — '010' narrows to the 0101/0102 range the way a trader expects.

claims.statement: When the query matches a commodity's name or code, every species under that commodity is listed; otherwise only the species whose own label matches are listed.
claims.quote:
Name or code hits the whole commodity, so every species under it stays in
// the results; otherwise only the species that match on their own.

claims.statement: A species is matched on the label the trader is shown, so its English common name is searchable as well as its scientific name.

claims.statement: Each row's Remove is a link-styled submit button reading 'Remove' with the row's name as visually hidden text (so it is announced as, for example, 'Remove Cow').
Remove is a form post carrying the CSRF crumb, never a link, so no GET can remove a commodity.
claims.quote:
A removal drops every line of one commodity group, so it submits the page
// form — the crumb travels with it and no GET can trigger it.

claims.statement: Removing a commodity row drops every commodity line (every species) of that commodity; a commodity index that does not name a selected commodity is refused with a 400 before anything changes.
Removing a species row drops that one commodity line and keeps the rest of its commodity; a line index that is missing or not under a species-listed commodity is refused with a 400.
After a removal the user returns to the Commodity details page while any line is left, or to the commodity search page when the last line was removed (keeping the change context).
Removing a commodity also removes any animal identifier records held on its lines, because the whole line is dropped.
claims.quote: await state.reconcileEntriesAt(request, h, ['commodityLines'], lineKey, kept)
claims.note: Identifier records are stored under each line (evaluation.js groups unit under line), so dropping the line drops them. No confirmation step is shown before removal.

claims.statement: Quantity validation runs per species line, so each line with a problem gets its own error message and error summary link that focuses its field; entered values are kept (trimmed) on the re-rendered page.
Count-drop rule: once the quantities are otherwise valid, a line that already holds animal identifier records cannot be given a number of animals lower than the number of records.
The count-drop error reads 'You have <N> identifier record(s) for <species> but entered <M> animal(s). Remove identifier records or keep the higher count.', pluralised by count.
claims.quote: `You have ${plural(records, 'identifier record')} for ${species} but entered ${plural(entered, 'animal')}. Remove identifier records or keep the higher count.`
